correctness.rationale: For all N>=3, 2<=M<=N-1 and 0<rho<1, the source payoff difference reduces by multinomial summation to binomial(n,h) z^h[(x+y)^s-(x+rho*y)^s]. Fixing z makes the bracket strictly decrease with x; maximizing z^h(1-z)^s gives the unique boundary maximizer and exact H. If x(0),z(0)>0 and cost>=L omega H, the ratio z/x is nonincreasing; its closed compact invariant slice excludes that unique maximizer, giving a strict trajectory-dependent negative bound and exponential z extinction even at equality. The limiting scalar cooperator-defector field has only isolated zeros, so asymptotically autonomous one-dimensional convergence applies. The adjacent ratio follows by exact factorial cancellation and a strictly monotone risk factor; its unique crossover and the 1/8 example are algebraically proved. Stirling proves large-N rates. An independent exact-rational multinomial enumeration passed 13,680 compositions and additional comparisons. Finite enumeration is not used as an infinite proof. Limits: no persistence claim below the ceiling or trajectories with x(0)=0.

value.rationale: The motivating work makes quorum severity and protective intervention costs central model questions and gives numerical bifurcation thresholds rather than an all-composition selective-advantage bound. This theorem provides a sharp computable no-protection-advantage cost barrier, exact global elimination at the otherwise nonuniform equality case, a nontrivial reversal showing higher quorums can sometimes improve possible incentives, and distinct extensive/fixed quorum large-group scaling. These are structural, natural parametric boundaries for a motivating public-goods model, not arbitrary numeric slices or claims of a new binomial mode.
